title: Dependency Mosaic: Cross-team Handshake Protocol and Readiness Scoreboard
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: cross-team dependencies (Eng/Design/Security/Infra) become visible too late in a cycle, causing last-minute scope cuts, unreliable rollouts, and unclear owner handoffs. Current signals (calendar syncs + readiness emails) are noisy and don't capture execution risk or required cutover steps.

Goal: deliver a lightweight, repeatable 'Dependency Mosaic'—a multi-dimensional readiness scoreboard plus a crisp handshake protocol that standardizes pre-handoff checks, automates gating signals, and surfaces remediation actions to unblock delivery. The Mosaic will be adopted as the canonical dependency status for quarterly planning, sprint cutovers, and canary rollouts.

Scope: prototype scoreboard UI tile in Console (project-level), a small webhook-based readiness API for teams to push status, Slack handshake flow templates, and a PM-run playbook that defines signal levels and escalation paths. Does NOT include automatic enforcement of capacity or autoscale changes (out of scope for this ticket).

Why different: rather than a binary blocker list, Mosaic encodes multiple axes (design acceptance, API contract stability, infra capacity, security sign-off, test coverage) into a 0-100 readiness index with color-coded badges and suggested remediation playbooks. It is intentionally human-interpretable and machine-readable (simple JSON webhook), enabling dashboards, email digests, and automated cutover gating in subsequent work.
acceptance_criteria: A project-level Mosaic tile renders in Console with a computed readiness score and breakdown by axis
Teams can POST readiness payloads to the new API and see reflected updates within 60s
Handshake checklist template exists with required signoffs for Eng, Design, Security, and Infra
Slack handshake flow sends a pre-cutover prompt and records an acknowledgement (who, when, comments)
A lightweight remediation task recommendation is generated when any axis falls below threshold
Documentation (Confluence) and PM playbook published and linked from the ticket
tasks: Design: small scoreboard tile mockups (DES) and badge states
Engineering: implement /api/v1/readiness POST endpoint + simple compute service
Infra: define capacity check queries and provide sample metrics for prototype
Security: define required signoff checklist items and acceptable evidence
PM: draft handshake flow, escalation rules, and rollout plan for pilot teams
DevEx: add Console routing to surface Mosaic tile on project overview
QA: test webhook flows, badge updates, time-to-update SLA <= 60s
Docs: create Confluence 'Dependency Mosaic Playbook' and onboarding checklist

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams treat the Mosaic as a checkbox rather than a diagnostic tool. Mitigation: require a free-text 'blocking reason' and run two-week retrospective on pilot usage
Risk: Badge drift if teams forget to POST updates. Mitigation: add daily reminder digest and a lightweight CLI/SDK helper for common CI integrations
Risk: Security axis could be bottleneck. Mitigation: define 'acceptable evidence' tiers and allow provisional signoff with follow-up tasks
Risk: Console performance impact. Mitigation: tile is readonly and reads precomputed scores; backend compute runs on a 30s cadence to avoid live query spikes
